subject: Mutual action & TTFT streaming benchmark — Catalyst pilot
messages:
From: Samir Joshi <samir@catalyst.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot benchmarking and MAP for streaming chat latency

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Catalyst is ready to run a short pilot focused on streaming chat quality and latency so we can decide whether to go with Redwood Dedicated for our production traffic. High level asks from our side:

- A mutual action plan (MAP) that lists milestone owners and dates leading to an agreement. Our target close is end of June.
- A performance benchmarking plan that measures TTFT (time-to-first-token) and streaming latency across realistic concurrency up to 50 concurrent sessions, plus throughput numbers (tokens/sec).
- Initial p50/p95/p99 targets and test methodology so we can validate fairness of the comparison.

Some constraints: our service needs p95 TTFT under ~700ms for 1–25 concurrency, and we'd like to validate behavior up to 50 concurrent users. We will provide a prompt corpus (~2k prompts) and sample user sessions. Also note we are evaluating cost per token/throughput for a 30-day estimate.

Can you send a proposed MAP + benchmark plan and an initial timeline?

—Samir
Samir Joshi
CTO, Catalyst Labs
samir@catalyst.ai
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <samir@catalyst.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot benchmarking and MAP for streaming chat latency

Samir —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is an initial MAP (RDW-Catalyst-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a concise benchmarking plan. High-level summary below; the MAP contains owners, acceptance criteria, and dates.

MAP highlights (proposed)
- Kickoff & data receipt (you): target 2027-05-21
- Baseline benchmark run (Redwood): 2027-05-21 — produce p50/p95/p99 TTFT + per-token streaming latency at concurrency sweep [1,10,25,50]
- Follow-up quality eval & cost estimate (joint): 2027-05-24
- Decision checkpoint + contract terms (you + legal): 2027-06-02
- Close target: 2027-06-30

Benchmark plan (summary)
- Scenarios: single-turn chat (median prompt length ~45 tokens), multi-turn sessions (up to 6 turns), and long context generation (1k token output).
- Measurements: TTFT measured from request accept to first streamed token; per-token streaming latency measured (first-byte + per-token intervals). Report p50/p95/p99 for each.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 10, 25, 50 concurrent sessions with steady state for 600s each.
- Throughput: tokens/sec and cost estimate normalized to your traffic profile.
- Model variants: Redwood-curated open model (quantized) vs. full FP16; we'll test both and report delta.
- Acceptance: p95 TTFT threshold you listed; quality regression checks via sample eval prompts you provide.

Attachments: RDW-Catalyst-MAP-v1.xlsx (milestones & owners)

Next steps: please share the prompt corpus and any compliance constraints (PII/HIPAA). Marcus (cc'd) will own the run plan; Rachel will coordinate commercial terms; Stephanie will be the escrow/contact for dedicated capacity questions.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Samir Joshi <samir@catalyst.ai>
Cc: rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot benchmarking and MAP for streaming chat latency

Samir / Kimberly —

Quick technical notes on measurement so we line up on definitions: please confirm these before we run.

1) TTFT definition: time from HTTP request reach (server recv timestamp) to the first streamed token byte delivered to client. We will log both server-side and client-observed first-byte times; report will include both numbers.

2) Streaming latency buckets: compute per-token deltas and aggregate to p50/p95/p99. We'll also report first-byte latency separately for cold vs warmed KV cache (we'll run a warm-up of 30 sessions).

3) Concurrency and batching: we will exercise Redwood Dedicated pool with controlled arrival rates to achieve the concurrency targets. Batching windows will be recorded; we'll provide the batch size distribution.

4) Model & run config: temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95, max_new_tokens=512; for deterministic comparability we'll run a seeded set with temperature=0.0 as well. Quantization profiles: 4-bit and FP16.

5) Artifacts: scripts (run_bench_v1.sh), log parsers, and the results CSV will be shared. We'll include a short README describing how to reproduce the run on your side.

If that's acceptable Samir, we'll schedule the baseline run once we have the corpus and permission to run against your test company account.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin — Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai
From: Samir Joshi <samir@catalyst.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: engops@catalyst.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot benchmarking and MAP for streaming chat latency

Thanks — this looks good. We've uploaded the evaluation corpus and prompt sets to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CatalystTestCorpus

Files you will use: catalyst_prompt_set_v1.json (contains session metadata), and a small golden sample set (100 prompts) for quality checks. We confirm p95 TTFT target of 700ms for 1–25 concurrency; above that we expect graceful degradation but please document behavior.

One ask: can you include a short run on Redwood Dedicated (reserved) vs Redwood-hosted so we can see delta in latency and cost? We are particularly interested if Dedicated reduces p95 TTFT by >20% at 25 concurrent sessions.

Also note: we need a short written note on compliance handling for the test data (no PHI in the corpus). We will not provide PHI for the pilot.

—Samir
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <samir@catalyst.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot benchmarking and MAP for streaming chat latency

Samir —

We ran the baseline benchmark today against the corpus you provided. Attached is streaming_results_v1.csv; below is a short summary (baseline = Redwood-hosted open model, warmed cache). Detailed run artifacts and scripts attached in the Drive link.

Summary — TTFT (first-token) and streaming latency — Redwood-hosted (warmed cache)
- Concurrency = 1: p50 TTFT = 120 ms, p95 = 210 ms, p99 = 430 ms
- Concurrency = 10: p50 TTFT = 160 ms, p95 = 360 ms, p99 = 760 ms
- Concurrency = 25: p50 TTFT = 230 ms, p95 = 620 ms, p99 = 1,250 ms
- Concurrency = 50: p50 TTFT = 420 ms, p95 = 1,100 ms, p99 = 2,300 ms

Streaming per-token median intervals (tokens/sec equivalent sample)
- Concurrency = 1: median per-token latency = 45 ms (≈22 tokens/sec)
- Concurrency = 25: median per-token latency = 58 ms (≈17 tokens/sec)

Dedicated delta (prelim run on a small 2-GPU Dedicated pool)
- At Concurrency = 25: p95 TTFT reduced from 620 ms -> 390 ms (~37% improvement)
- Cost estimate: Dedicated variant shows ~1.6x cost per token relative to hosted when amortized across reserved commit; we'll add precise numbers in the cost sheet.

Notes & next steps
- The p95 numbers at 1–25 concurrency meet Catalyst's 700ms target; p99 at 25 is above threshold (1.25s) and we should discuss whether to include p99 in acceptance criteria or rely on p95.
- We recommend a follow-up run with quantized 4-bit model and a longer warm-up (2k session warm-up) to see p99 improvements.
- Proposed next meeting: 2027-05-24 to review full report and cost sheet.

Attachments: streaming_results_v1.csv (per-run CSV), RDW-Catalyst-MAP-v1.xlsx (updated)

If that timing works, Rachel will follow up with the commercial proposal and Stephanie will scope Dedicated sizing options in parallel.

Thanks — looking forward to the 5/24 review.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
